chunks: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir, who said:
I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام in Mecca when a man from al-Madīnah came to him. He said to him, “Who accompanied you?” He said, “No one accompanied me.”
So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to him, “Indeed, had I instructed you beforehand, I would have improved your manners.”
Then he said, “One is a shayṭān, two are two shayṭāns, three are companions, and four are fellow travelers.”

key_terms.شَيْطَانٌ: shayṭān, used here to censure solitary travel

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach about traveling alone?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the etiquette of travel and discourages traveling alone. Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام presents companionship in travel as proper conduct and frames isolation as blameworthy, emphasizing safety, sociability, and disciplined manners.
